solutions.warehouse.title: AMR and warehouse robotics | Professional Robotics
solutions.warehouse.description: AMRs, pallet-handling robots and software to manage a fleet of mixed brands: site assessment, one-route pilot, WMS and 1C integration, SLA-backed service.
solutions.warehouse.name: Warehouse robotics
solutions.warehouse.lead: You can buy an AMR from any supplier. The hard part comes later: robots must be connected to your WMS or 1C, spread across routes and kept online. We deploy software that manages a fleet of AMRs of different brands, and put it on robots you already have or ones we select.
solutions.warehouse.lead2: It is better to start with one route, not the whole warehouse.
solutions.warehouse.primaryCta.label: Select a warehouse solution
solutions.warehouse.secondaryCta.label: The fleet dispatcher
solutions.warehouse.hero.routeLabel: Route diagram: the robot drives a loop between the dock, the racks and shipping
solutions.warehouse.hero.routeFoot: Start with one route: the effect shows fast and the investment is small.
solutions.warehouse.heads.paths: Where to start: three ways in.
solutions.warehouse.heads.pathsLead: The robot is the carrier here; the product is the software that runs it. So you can come to us with a fleet or without one.
solutions.warehouse.heads.dispatcherLead: Tasks come from your systems, and robots get them through the platform. The robot’s brand should not change how you run the warehouse.
solutions.warehouse.heads.directionsLead: By operation, not by brand. The whole order path through a warehouse is shown on the industry page.
solutions.warehouse.heads.economyLead: A spec sheet will not show payback: it depends on your warehouse’s routes, shifts and peaks.
solutions.warehouse.paths.items.0.title: You already have AMRs or pallet-handling robots.
solutions.warehouse.paths.items.0.text: We connect the fleet to one platform: a shared task queue, routes, monitoring. The condition is access to the robot’s interface: VDA 5050, an API or the maker’s SDK. We check it before work starts.
solutions.warehouse.paths.items.1.title: No fleet yet.
solutions.warehouse.paths.items.1.text: We select the robot type for your load, aisles and floor, and launch one route as a pilot. You can rent a robot instead of buying it.
solutions.warehouse.paths.items.2.title: You need integration with your systems.
solutions.warehouse.paths.items.2.text: Tasks from WMS or 1C, statuses back, charging control, your own reports. We write it for your process within the platform.
solutions.warehouse.problems.items.0.tex: Developed economies have 500–800 robots per 10,000 employees; Russia’s target for 2030 is 145. Only 3% of warehouses are fully automated with robots.
solutions.warehouse.problems.items.1.cap: of surveyed companies plan to use AMRs
solutions.warehouse.problems.items.1.tex: In a survey of 112 respondents from 51 companies, 43% wanted to launch 2–5 mobile robot projects in 2025.
solutions.warehouse.problems.items.2.cap: the time in which investment pays back, by the study’s estimate
solutions.warehouse.problems.items.2.tex: Barriers named by the same study: the cost of entry, immature IT infrastructure, a shortage of specialists.

solutions.warehouse.dispatcher.robots.it: AMR beside the picker · brand C
solutions.warehouse.dispatcher.note: Connection is easier if the robot supports VDA 5050: an open specification for communication between a master control system and mobile robots from different makers (VDA and VDMA, version 3.0.0 of March 2026). If it does not, we connect through the maker’s API or SDK. What is available for your model, we check at the site assessment.
solutions.warehouse.dispatcher.legend: The diagram is illustrative: brands A, B and C stand for robots from different makers.
solutions.warehouse.directions.items.0.t: They move pallets horizontally: dock, rack, shipping area. The simplest entry: the route repeats and the warehouse is not rebuilt.
solutions.warehouse.directions.items.0.f: floor surface, aisle width, thresholds and ramps
solutions.warehouse.directions.items.1.t: Goods come to the person: the robot brings the rack. Or the robot drives beside the picker and carries what has been picked.
solutions.warehouse.directions.items.2.t: A robot arm takes boxes off a pallet or builds a pallet for shipping. Heavy repetitive work leaves the dock.
solutions.warehouse.directions.items.3.t: Mobile robots handle the order flow, dynamic storage, sorting and inventory. We add them once the first routes are running.
solutions.warehouse.directions.items.3.l: The whole order path through a warehouse
solutions.warehouse.directionsNote: Safety around people is described by the international standard ISO 3691-4: detecting a person, limiting speed, stopping. We clarify the requirements and certification for your warehouse at the site assessment.
solutions.warehouse.econ.how.title: What the calculation is made of
solutions.warehouse.econ.how.items.items: how many kilometers per shift people and forklifts cover on routes that can be handed to a robot
how many shifts the warehouse runs and how much the load jumps between peak and low season; we count by the peak, not the average
the share of picking errors and cargo damage before and after
robot, charging, integration with WMS or 1C, training, SLA-backed service: all in one estimate, not in parts after launch
solutions.warehouse.econ.market.title: What others have achieved
solutions.warehouse.econ.market.rows.ite: The time in which investment in warehouse robotics pays back, by the estimate of the surveyed companies.
Output per employee grew from about 18 to 32+ tonnes. The company’s own claim.
One employee instead of three on the operation, 70–80 → 300–350 units per hour. The company’s own claim.
solutions.warehouse.econ.note: These are other companies’ deployments, and the figures are the companies’ own claims that we did not verify independently. A precise calculation comes on your routes after the site assessment.
solutions.warehouse.econ.link.label: See all deployments
solutions.warehouse.vendorsLead: We connect robots from these and other manufacturers to one platform. We select equipment for the load, aisles and floor surface, not from a catalog.
solutions.warehouse.pilot.items.0.title: Warehouse assessment
solutions.warehouse.pilot.items.0.text: Flows, aisles, floor surface, thresholds and ramps. We choose the route where a robot pays off soonest.
solutions.warehouse.pilot.items.1.title: One route on our software
solutions.warehouse.pilot.items.1.text: A robot (yours or one we select) works one route at your normal load, and the warehouse does not stop. Tasks come from your WMS or 1C.
solutions.warehouse.pilot.items.2.title: Integration and scale
solutions.warehouse.pilot.items.2.text: We connect the other routes and systems. Robots of different brands work in one window.
solutions.warehouse.pilot.items.3.title: Service
solutions.warehouse.pilot.items.3.text: Fleet monitoring, tickets and maintenance run under an SLA.
solutions.warehouse.form.title: Which route to start with in your warehouse?
solutions.warehouse.form.lead: Describe the warehouse: area, loads, shifts, whether you already have robots. We will suggest a pilot route and a way to connect.
